clue.text: A swimmer confined to bed opened up

indicators.note: the swimmer is shut up inside the word for a bed, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: taken as written
a roach is a freshwater fish, so a swimmer

explanation.surface: A fish has been kept in bed and someone has opened it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimmer' is a crossword favourite for a fish rather than a person; 'confined to' splits the bed word round it.
explanation.definitionFit: To broach a subject or a cask is to open it up, raise it or tap it.

clue.text: Penniless beggar

definitions.meaning: the verb, to ruin someone financially

explanation.definitionFit: Insolvent describes the penniless; to beggar someone is to ruin them financially.

clue.text: Done with 24. due to lack of attention

parts.note: over means finished or done
the answer to 24 down is a faculty such as vision, one of the five

explanation.surface: Someone finished with sense, blaming carelessness.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 down is SENSE; sight is one example of a sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An oversight is a mistake made through failing to notice something.

clue.text: Confident about a Shakespearian role

parts.note: C, from circa, means about
King Lear is a title role by Shakespeare

explanation.surface: An actor feels sure about landing a Shakespeare part.
explanation.definitionFit: To be clear about something is to be sure, certain of it.

clue.text: A romance turned one on, bringing delight

indicators.note: the romance is turned round, so read backwards

parts.note: a tale is a story, a romance
I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A love affair turned someone on and made them happy.
explanation.definitionFit: Elation is great happiness and exhilaration.

clue.text: Many a Northerner exhibits charm

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, standing for many in crosswords
taken as written
a Scot comes from the north of Britain

explanation.surface: A great many people from the North display a lucky charm.
explanation.definitionFit: A mascot is a lucky charm, a figure or object kept to bring good fortune.

clue.text: Meant to transform the exterior of some home

indicators.note: the rearranged letters form the outside, with the other piece inside
the letters of meant are to be transformed into a new order

parts.note: part means some, a portion

explanation.surface: Someone intends to do up the outside of their house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to transform' gives AMENT, the anagram of the first word; 'the exterior of' wraps those letters round the portion word, splitting after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: An apartment is a flat, a set of rooms to live in.

clue.text: An announcer in tears?

parts.note: a town announcer, or literally one who weeps

explanation.definitionFit: A town official shouting proclamations; read literally, a person who weeps.

clue.text: Catch up the German boat

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is written upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to net is to catch
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: Grab the German vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses NET to TEN in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A tender is a small boat ferrying people or supplies to a larger ship.

clue.text: Local news broadcaster

explanation.surface: A local radio presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle chatter about neighbours, and the person who spreads it about.

clue.text: Critical about egghead member of the family

indicators.note: the word for critical goes round the other piece, so it sits outside

parts.note: nice in its old sense means exacting or finely discriminating, as in a nice distinction
the head of the word egg is its first letter E

explanation.surface: Someone picky about an intellectual relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' looks like an intellectual but gives E, the first letter of egg; 'about' puts NICE round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a brother's or sister's daughter, so a relative.

clue.text: Love to ordain a change

indicators.note: the letters of the words before are to be changed, that is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Love leads someone to ordain a change in their life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a change' rearranges the nine letters of TO ORDAIN A; the second 'a' does double surface duty but supplies its letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is deep love and worship.

clue.text: Checks taxes — not for the first time!

parts.note: re- as a prefix means again, so not for the first time
to tax something is to put a strain on it, so taxes means strains

explanation.surface: Someone checks a tax return again, exclaiming it is not the first time.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain is to hold back or keep in check.

clue.text: The Irish will go after a shirt that's casual yet crisp

indicators.note: the Irish piece is placed after the shirt piece in the answer

parts.note: a T-shirt is a casual shirt, giving T
Erse is the Irish Gaelic language

explanation.surface: Irish people will chase a shirt that is informal yet smart.
explanation.walkthrough: ERSE is the old name for Irish Gaelic.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisp reply is a short, brusque one.

clue.text: Beast with a club — a lump of metal

parts.note: a pig is a beast or farm animal
an iron is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A creature armed with a club is described as a lump of metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Pig iron is crude iron cast into oblong lumps called pigs.

clue.text: Phone without hesitation about the last application by a builder

indicators.note: the phone word stands outside, holding the rest within

parts.note: to ring is to phone
the end is the last part
er is a sound of hesitation, and about merely joins it to the last

explanation.surface: Call without delay about the final job for a builder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking: the phone word encloses the rest. Rendering is a builder's coat of plaster on a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Rendering is a coat of plaster or cement applied by a builder to a wall.

clue.text: A copper once used by the cook

definitions.meaning: an early nickname for a policeman, after Sir Robert Peel
a kitchen tool for taking the skin off vegetables

explanation.surface: An old-time policeman was useful in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: Peelers, like Bobbies, were London police named after Sir Robert Peel, who founded the force.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a Victorian policeman, and a kitchen gadget for stripping vegetable skins.

clue.text: Band involved in awful melee is to be corrected

indicators.note: the band gets mixed up in an awful jumble with the other word, so all letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as fodder
taken as written as fodder

explanation.surface: A band caught up in a nasty brawl needs to be put right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in awful' mixes BAND with MELEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Emendable means capable of being amended, open to correction.

clue.text: "Let my due feet never fail to walk the ___ cloister's pale" (Milton)

definitions.text: "Let my due feet never fail to walk the ___ cloister's pale" (Milton)

parts.words: "Let my due feet never fail to walk the ___ cloister's pale" (Milton)
parts.note: the missing word of the line from Il Penseroso describes a cloister given to learning

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank quotation from Milton's Il Penseroso.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloisters are places of quiet study, so the adjective means devoted to learning.

clue.text: Bearing with fish smell

parts.note: S, south, is a compass bearing
a tench is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A fish gives off a distinctive smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A stench is a strong, foul smell.

clue.text: A simple catalogue

parts.note: simple here is a noun, a medicinal plant, so a book listing them

explanation.definitionFit: A herbal is a book describing plants and their medicinal uses; simples are medicinal herbs.

clue.text: Huff about bond being invalid

indicators.note: the word for huff goes round the bond, placing it inside

parts.note: to huff is to blow or breathe hard, to pant
a tie is a bond

explanation.surface: Someone takes offence over a bond that turns out legally void.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invalid' reads as an adjective (void) but is the noun, a sick person.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient is a sick person under a doctor's care, an invalid.

clue.text: RAF officer demanding entrance

parts.note: PO is a pilot officer in the Royal Air Force
stern means strict, demanding

explanation.surface: An air force officer demands to be let in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demanding' reads as a verb but is the adjective, strict.
explanation.definitionFit: A postern is a back or side gate, a secondary way in.

clue.text: They come below the knees in neat youngsters

definitions.meaning: the backs of the lower legs
neat is an old word for cattle, so their young

explanation.surface: Smart children wear something below the knee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' looks like tidy but is an old word for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Lower leg muscles, and young cattle.

clue.text: This could well lead to a wedding

definitions.text: This could well lead to a wedding

parts.words: This could well lead to a wedding
parts.note: read literally, the walkway down the middle of a church leads the bride to the altar

explanation.definitionFit: A bride walks down the central passage of a church to be married.

clue.text: Reason a nurse takes directions

parts.note: SEN is a State Enrolled Nurse
S and E are compass directions, south and east

explanation.surface: A nurse follows instructions for a good reason.
explanation.walkthrough: SEN, State Enrolled Nurse, was a British nursing grade.
explanation.definitionFit: Sense is sound judgement, reason.

clue.text: Discerned to be faulty, so cancelled

indicators.note: the letters of the word are faulty, so wrongly ordered and to be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A decision was seen to be flawed and so revoked.
explanation.definitionFit: To rescind a law or order is to revoke or annul it.

clue.text: Trendy place to feed in

parts.note: in means fashionable
to put is to place

explanation.surface: A fashionable spot to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Input is data or material fed into a system.

clue.text: Few show 3

definitions.note: the answer to clue 3, meaning confident or free of blame

parts.note: V, Roman five, a small number, stands for few
to indicate is to show or point out

explanation.surface: A handful of people show something unclear.
explanation.walkthrough: '3' refers to the answer of 3 down, CLEAR, here as a verb meaning to free from blame.
explanation.definitionFit: To vindicate someone is to clear them of suspicion or blame.

clue.text: Spaniard — a bit of a wimp — a blockhead

indicators.note: only a piece of the following words is taken, the letters running across them

explanation.surface: A Spaniard is called a bit of a wimp and an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit of' takes letters from wimP A BLOckhead.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo is a common Spanish man's name, as in Picasso.

clue.text: Transport and plant round lake

indicators.note: the plant goes round the lake piece, so it sits outside

parts.note: sedge is a grass-like marsh plant
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: Vehicles and greenery surround a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A sledge is a vehicle on runners for travel over snow.

clue.text: Woolly-minded needlewomen

parts.note: woolly-minded reads as muddled but means minds set on wool, women working with needles and yarn

explanation.definitionFit: People who make garments from wool with needles naturally think about wool.
